question.text: Under FEMA's classification framework (and ignoring PIO status for the moment), an Indian citizen who holds an Indian passport and has been residing in Dubai for the past 3 years (clearly satisfying the residency test for a person resident outside India) wishes to invest in Indian securities. His father was born in pre-partition Lahore (undivided India). Which FEMA residential classification applies to this individual for investment purposes?

answer.text: He is an NRI (Non-Resident Indian) under FEMA, because he is an Indian citizen who is a person resident outside India
He is a person resident in India for FEMA purposes, since Indian citizens are always treated as residents
He has no defined residential status under FEMA, since his father was born in undivided India
He is an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) under FEMA, because he has lived abroad for 3 years

explanation.text: The Logic: Under FEMA, residential status is determined by where the person resides, not by ancestry. A "Non-Resident Indian" (NRI) is an Indian citizen who is a person resident outside India. The stem confirms Indian citizenship and 3 years of residence in Dubai (well over the 182-day threshold), so he is an NRI under FEMA. PIO is a separate concept that applies to foreign passport holders of Indian origin and is therefore not the FEMA residential classification for this Indian citizen. The Trap: The "always treated as residents" option is wrong because FEMA's resident test is residence-based, not citizenship-based. The "no defined status" option is wrong because ancestry does not remove residential status. The OCI option is wrong because OCI is a citizenship/visa status, not a FEMA residential classification, and is not conferred merely by living abroad. The audit flagged the original item because the previous explanation claimed PIO status is only for foreign passport holders, which is not the workbook's exact wording on the cited pages. Note: The original stem mixed FEMA residential classification with the separate PIO ancestry concept, allowing PIO-based distractors to be contested. The stem now asks specifically under FEMA classification (and explicitly sets aside PIO), making the NRI classification uniquely correct under NISM Series X-A pp.308-310, which defines NRI as an Indian citizen who is a person resident outside India.
